title: QuickCards: contextual micro-guides for batching + cache policy decisions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact, contextual UI component (QuickCard) shown inline in the Console that gives engineers bite-sized recommendations for batching and caching settings. Each QuickCard summarizes recommended changes, expected latency/cost impact, confidence level, and suggested guardrails or canary rollout parameters.
acceptance_criteria: QuickCard appears on per-route and per-model config pages and is discoverable without overwhelming the main form
Each card shows: recommendation summary, delta metrics (latency, cost), confidence band, and a one-click 'Apply as preset' action
Prototype includes responsive layouts for narrow side panel and full-page inspector
Design includes error/blocked states when policy conflicts with route constraints and clear next steps
Accessibility: cards follow color contrast WCAG AA and are keyboard navigable with screen reader labels
comments: 2025-02-21: Kickoff with PM/Eng. Agreed scope: surface top-2 recommendations only, avoid replacing full config editor.

2025-02-24: Engineering review (K. Romero): suggested adding 'compatibility check' that simulates whether kv-cache preset works with current model quantization; flagged potential perf regression for short seqs.
2025-02-26: PM feedback (L. Novak): prioritize canary rollout CTA and explicit indication of whether change requires model-reload vs runtime-only toggle.
2025-03-01: Prototype 0.1 shared in design critique. Design feedback: reduce verbosity in mobile; swap risk icon for confidence meter.
2025-03-03: Security review requested by SRE (R. Gupta): ensure audit trail links included, and note where KMS-protected models cannot cache across tenants. Follow-up created.
2025-03-04: Accessibility pass by D. Chen: updated focus states and aria-labels; added textual confidence description alongside color indicators. Ready for stakeholder review.
design_decisions: Keep QuickCards compact (max 3 lines of body) with expandable details to avoid interrupting power users
Show delta metrics as sparklines + absolute % change to make impact scannable
Provide two levels of action: 'Apply as preset' (safe, reversible) and 'Open advanced editor'
Treat guardrails as non-editable suggestions by default; allow advanced users to override after a warning and automatic canary rollout
Integrate with Console audit logs: every 'Apply' action creates a config-change event linked in card confirmation toast
tradeoffs_and_risks: Hiding too much detail may frustrate advanced users — mitigated by explicit 'advanced editor' path
Automated recommendations could be misaligned with niche workloads (e.g., extreme short-sequence inference) — addressed by confidence band and simulation note
Applying presets without sufficient canary coverage could cause regressions — default to a 10% canary and opt-out for teams that cannot canary due to capacity
Extra DB/compute to run recommendation simulations — plan to run lightweight heuristics in the Console, heavier simulations in periodic background jobs
prototype_notes: Prototype 0.1: three QuickCard variants — Cost-first, Latency-first, Safety-first. Shown in right inspector for a sample 'chat-completion' route.
Prototype includes a micro-interaction: hovering a metric shows a tooltip with underlying assumptions (batch size distribution, typical prefix length)
Mobile layout collapses metrics into an accordion to preserve vertical space
Visuals include a traffic-light style confidence bar and a secondary 'why this recommendation?' link opening a short modal
review_feedback_summary: PM: Ensure QuickCards don't auto-apply; user must confirm. Add last-simulated timestamp to the card.
Engineering: Add compatibility check for KV cache + quantized model; flag unsupported combos as 'Not recommended' rather than suggesting changes.
Security: Card must warn when recommendation touches data residency or cross-tenant cache boundaries; link to audit policy.
Design: Reduce copy length, add microcopy for 'confidence' and 'expected variance'
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi Figma with updated microcopy and canary defaults (due 2025-03-07)
Add backend spec for 'simulate-impact' endpoint and compatibility checks (ENG- follow-up ticket)
Create an experiment plan with metric definitions (P99 latency, tokens / USD) and guardrail rollback criteria
Schedule cross-functional review with SRE and PM on 2025-03-10
notes: Empathy note: most users will accept a small latency increase for large per-token savings; surface explicit per-token cost to help decision-making.
Consider later adding a 'Explain' mode that surfaces sanitized example prompts showing when cache helps vs harms.
Metrics team requested event hooks for 'recommendation_shown' and 'recommendation_applied' to measure adoption
